purpose: Development-only fixed holdout scenarios, not training examples. Review questions are never sent to the coach.

cases.title: Rushed cold prospect

payload.context: Unscheduled outbound to a support executive. No verified pain or prior engagement.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi Morgan, Omri from Salesforce. I’m calling about your support operation.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: You caught me on my way into a board meeting. What is this about?

cases.manual_review: Does advice respect the time boundary while establishing relevance?

cases.title: Send me an email

payload.context: Unscheduled outbound. Buyer has not agreed to discovery. The CRM already contains the buyer’s verified work email.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I had an idea about simplifying service handoffs.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Please email it. I can’t do a call today.

cases.manual_review: Does it respect the boundary without more qualification or asking for an email already known?

cases.title: Interested cold prospect

payload.context: Outbound call; initially unexpected. Account research contains no quantified loss.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I wondered whether the manual handoff after a sale is becoming difficult.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Actually, yes. We’ve been trying to fix that since spring. I have a few minutes if you have a concrete idea.

cases.manual_review: Does it pursue real interest rather than retreat or invent impact?

cases.title: Wrong stakeholder

payload.context: Outbound to an executive whose responsibilities were not verified.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I wanted to understand how your sales team prepares customer quotes.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That isn’t my team. I look after facilities, not sales.

cases.manual_review: Does it avoid irrelevant discovery, with an optional low-effort redirect or exit?

cases.title: Existing Salesforce customer

payload.context: Known Sales Cloud customer. No approved expansion project or known product gap.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Omri from Salesforce here. Your team has been growing.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already use Salesforce and it works fine. I don’t want a replacement pitch.

cases.manual_review: Does it respect the installed footprint and actual objection without inventing dissatisfaction?

cases.title: Weak, non-material pain

payload.context: The buyer has described an occasional manual lookup, without measurable impact.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Is the lookup getting in the way of the team’s work?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It’s mildly annoying once in a while. Honestly, it’s not worth changing anything over.

cases.manual_review: Does it avoid inflating mild annoyance into urgency or a project?

cases.title: Meaningful pain

payload.context: No product selected. Buyer volunteers impact; no root cause is confirmed.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: How are the handoffs working now?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We lost two renewals after cases went between teams for days. Our service lead has asked me to get this sorted this month.

cases.manual_review: Does it recognize meaningful evidence and follow it without instantly prescribing a product?

cases.title: Vague buyer response

payload.context: Early expansion conversation; only general interest is known.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: What prompted you to look into this?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: A few things, really. It’s been a bit messy. Hard to explain.

cases.manual_review: Does it offer an accessible next move without manufacturing the problem?

cases.title: Skeptical buyer

payload.context: Existing customer. No approved implementation scope or verified implementation outcomes are supplied.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: There may be a way to reduce the manual work.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Every vendor says that. Last time we got six months of consultants and more work for my team.

cases.manual_review: Does it respond to the actual concern without a generic reassurance or guaranteed outcome?

cases.title: Direct product question

payload.context: Scheduled solution discussion. Customer uses Service Cloud. Order data is in a separate system; integrations and entitlements are unverified.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: The difficult part seems to be getting order information during a support case.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: What would MuleSoft actually do here? Is it replacing Service Cloud, and would our engineers still need to do anything?

cases.manual_review: Does it answer the question, explain mechanism and limits, and avoid unsupported integration promises?

cases.title: Next step already agreed

payload.context: Rep proposed a short workflow discussion with service operations. Buyer already supplied the right contact; no scheduling details are missing beyond sending options.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I can send a couple of times for a workflow discussion with your service operations manager.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Yes, send the options. I’ll include her. Thanks, Omri.

cases.manual_review: Does it close naturally without reselling or reconfirming the agreement?

cases.title: Scheduled discovery

payload.context: Thirty-minute discovery already scheduled at buyer request. Goal is understanding the workflow; no purchase or solution agreement yet.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Where should we start today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: The case screen works. It’s the delivery investigation afterward. People check orders, then carriers, then message the warehouse. We wanted help figuring out that part.

cases.manual_review: Does it follow the substantive thread rather than use a cold-call opener or rush to a demo?

cases.title: Buyer rejects the hypothesis

payload.context: Rep suggested a possible cause based on public growth signals. It remains an unverified hypothesis.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I wondered whether the higher contact volume was creating the backlog.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: No, volume is down. The backlog is a temporary audit hold, and compliance has already approved the release plan.

cases.manual_review: Does it update its understanding and avoid defending the rejected hypothesis or bypassing controls?

cases.title: Buyer still explaining

payload.context: Scheduled discovery. The buyer still has the floor; the final fragment is ongoing speech, not a completed turn.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Could you walk me through what happened?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: The store called us first, then we checked the shipment. That looked fine, but the warehouse had a different record, so I asked our lead to check. There’s another part to this, though—let me explain how the refund got involved…

cases.manual_review: Can it choose WAIT or LISTEN instead of interrupting a substantive unfinished answer?

cases.title: Clearly not a fit

payload.context: The buyer is a two-person local service business. No Salesforce requirement, scaling plan or unresolved workflow need is known.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Are you considering a different way to manage customer follow-up?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: No. We have a handful of regular customers, our current setup works, and we’re deliberately not growing. Please don’t book me into anything.

cases.manual_review: Does it accept the lack of fit and close without manufacturing a meeting?
